meeting_point: in the Public Garden in front of the George Washington statue facing Arlington Street
accessibility: mostly flat surfaces and little to no inclines. Stroller and wheelchair accessible.
description:
Take a trip through the Back Bay neighborhood and learn where Back Bay started, how it evolved, and where it is today. Discover why and how the Bay was filled, and hear about the homes of its Victorian residents and their servants. Learn what made Back Bay such an engineering marvel in its time.

On this tour, explore why the filling of the bay was considered the most ambitious civil engineering achievement in nineteenth-century America, and uncover how it was a landmark event of urban planning in every sense of the term.

- Guided 90 minute outdoor tour exploring Boston's urban landscape
- 0.9 mile tour at a moderate pace, stopping at various sites along the tour
